summary: The order-submit failures are caused by degradation of the external exchange partner api.exchange-partner.example, reached via exchange-gateway (H1, confidence 0.72, medium). exchange-gateway's outbound calls to that host began timing out at ~10:58-11:01Z (upstream latency ~75x step, error rate stepping to ~44-48%), its circuit breaker tripped at 11:03:26Z, and order-service's placeOrder path then returned 504s at ~31% with a ~30x p99 step. The reporter's deploy hypothesis is decisively excluded: order-service v2.15.2 was rolled back at 11:16Z and the failure persisted unchanged (~31% error, ~5000-5400ms p99) for ~96 minutes afterwards, and the gateway's degradation started before order-service's first error and includes 146 op=quoteSnapshot timeouts that do not originate from the order-submit path. Shared-component exhaustion (H4) and the pricing-engine config change (H3) are rejected on direct metric flatness and timing, respectively. Confidence is medium rather than high because the partner itself has has_telemetry:false, so the conclusion rests on exclusion of internal causes plus log attribution rather than positive partner-side evidence.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External exchange partner (api.exchange-partner.example) degradation is the root cause
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external exchange API reached via exchange-gateway began timing out/returning 503 at ~10:58-11:01Z (op=placeOrder and op=quoteSnapshot). exchange-gateway's calls to it fail, its upstream_latency blows up ~75x, its circuit breaker trips, and order-service's placeOrder path (which calls exchange-gateway) then returns 504s at ~31%. Negative evidence is now exhaustive across the internal change surface: the only recorded deploy (order-service v2.15.2, rolled back 11:16Z) and the only recorded config change (cfg-2290, 100 min pre-onset) are both excluded by timing/persistence; and exchange-gateway's entire ERROR stream is attributed to the single external host api.exchange-partner.example (all 309 WARN+ matches, 163 placeOrder + 146 quoteSnapshot; zero other host values; zero 'upstream error' matches). The residual gateway error rate (~44% vs ~31%) is explained by the gateway offering in additional traffic (quoteSnapshot) that order-service does not consume.

causal_chain.claim: External exchange partner API degrades at ~10:58-11:00Z (connect timeouts, then 503s); the vendor-side event is invisible to telemetry (has_telemetry:false)

exchange-gateway's outbound calls to host=api.exchange-partner.example fail: connect timeouts on op=placeOrder (163) and op=quoteSnapshot (146), then exchange-api returns 503 (161 occurrences, first 11:02:20Z, still 25 in the 12:40-12:58Z slice)

exchange-gateway latency p99 steps ~129ms -> ~4528ms (log-scan-independent metric: upstream_latency_ms 117-122ms -> ~8900-9750ms, ~75x) and error rate ~0.2% -> ~38.6% (upstream_error_rate 0.29-0.31% -> 44-48%); circuit breaker OPEN for exchange-api at 11:03:26Z with failure ratio 0.47

order-service's placeOrder path (downstream http edge to exchange-gateway) times out; all 349 order-service ERROR logs are the single signature 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)'
order-service error rate steps 0.2% -> ~31% and p99 ~150ms -> ~5000ms+ at the 11:00Z bucket, scoped to placeOrder; order-service's own db_pool and cpu are flat (13.6-14.4 in use, 39-40.7% cpu)

order-service v2.15.2 is rolled back at 11:16Z yet error rate stays ~31% and p99 ~5000-5400ms through 12:52Z, and the gateway remains degraded through 12:58Z — consistent with an origin outside the internal change surface

assumptions: The external partner's own state at 11:00Z is unobservable (has_telemetry:false) — no positive partner-side evidence exists; the conclusion rests on exclusion of internal causes (F5, F13-F28 flat) plus rollback ineffectiveness.
exchange-gateway's connect timeouts are causally prior to its 503s rather than a local gateway fault.

The gateway's residual ~44% error rate vs order-service's ~31% reflects gateway traffic mix (quoteSnapshot path not consumed by order-service) rather than a second degraded upstream — F31 (0 'upstream error' matches, only api.exchange-partner.example host values in 12:40-12:58Z) and the unchanged 44-48% banding of upstream_error_rate support the one-victim reading, but this is inference from logs, not a per-target metric split.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.15.2 'idempotency keys on order submit' introduced the defect (reporter's suspicion)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 10:48Z release of order-service v2.15.2 added idempotency-key handling to order submit; on ~30% of submits it holds the request long enough (lock/retry/duplicate-detection path) to blow the timeout budget toward exchange-gateway, producing 504s on placeOrder and a 30x p99 step.

causal_chain.claim: order-service v2.15.2 deployed 10:48Z changing the order-submit code path (idempotency keys)
New idempotency logic slows or serializes the placeOrder path, extending call duration toward exchange-gateway
order-service error rate steps to ~31% and p99 to ~5000ms at the 11:00Z bucket, scoped to placeOrder only
The failure surfaces at exchange-gateway as exchange-api 503s / partner timeouts because the gateway is waiting on a slow caller

assumptions: The new idempotency-key logic extends request duration or causes duplicate-submit retries against exchange-gateway — no finding shows this code behaviour; it is inferred only from the deploy summary.
order-service's ERROR logs faithfully record timeouts but do not establish which side timed out.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: F15 is decisive: error rate stayed ~31% and p99 ~5000-5400ms for ~96 minutes after the 11:16Z rollback, so the failure did not abate when v2.15.2 was removed. F6/F29 show exchange-gateway degrading BEFORE order-service's first error (11:01:25Z vs 11:02:45Z) with failures attributed to the external host api.exchange-partner.example, including 146 op=quoteSnapshot timeouts that do not originate from the order-submit path. F5 shows no local resource step in order-service (pool 13.6-14.4, cpu ~40%). The release precedes onset, but the symptom outlives it and its mechanism is partner-side.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Silent resource exhaustion on a shared component (ledger-db / kafka / redis-cache) outside the change surface
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared component (ledger-db, kafka or redis-cache — all flagged shared:true in order-service's blast radius) hit resource exhaustion at ~11:00Z without any versioned change, and the resulting stalls propagated into order-service as 504s. This alternative now has to be read as heavily damaged: ledger-db pool/cpu/slow-query, kafka replication/throughput/cpu and redis-cache cpu are all flat across the onset, and exchange-gateway's degradation is attributed exclusively to the external partner host, which shared-component exhaustion would not explain. It is retained only as the internal-infrastructure alternative, at low confidence, because no internal infra event feed (node restarts/drains, scaling) was queried.
ranked_hypotheses.root_cause_service: shared component in order-service blast radius (ledger-db / kafka / redis-cache)

causal_chain.claim: A shared component in order-service's blast radius (ledger-db, kafka or redis-cache) hits an internal infra event (failover, node drain, disk fill) at ~11:00Z
Resources exhaust there without any versioned/config change — F13 shows the change surface is only the v2.15.2 deploy and cfg-2290, and F8 shows no change in the preceding 18h
Calls through the affected path stall and surface as 504s on the order-submit path

assumptions: An invisible internal infra event (node drain, failover, disk fill) could exist without a versioned deploy or config record record — F13 only excludes versioned/config changes, and internal infra event feeds were never queried.
ledger-db disk_used_pct and replication_lag_ms were never queried (gap), so disk-fill/replica-lag on ledger-db is not fully excluded.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Every queried shared-component signal is flat through the 11:00Z onset: ledger-db connections_active 60.22-63.07 (F19), ledger-db cpu ~29-30% (F20), ledger-db slow_queries ~1/min and slightly LOWER during the incident (F21), kafka under_replicated_partitions 0.0 in every bucket and messages_in_per_s ~2500 flat (F22), kafka cpu flat ~34-36% (F23), redis-cache cpu flat ~22% (F24), market-data-service p99 flat ~40ms (F25). Mechanistically decisive: exchange-gateway's entire ERROR stream names the external host api.exchange-partner.example and nothing else (F29, F30, F31), and order-service's only error signature is the exchange-gateway/placeOrder 504 (F3) — a shared ledger-db/kafka/redis stall would surface on other callers and other endpoints, and would not produce partner-host-attributed gateway timeouts. Also no change record exists for these components (F13).

ranked_hypotheses.title: pricing-engine config change cfg-2290 (shorter quote cache TTL) is the trigger
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 09:20Z pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 change reduced quote cache hit rate, increasing load/latency through pricing-engine -> market-data-service / redis-cache, which propagated into order-service submit latency and 504s.

causal_chain.claim: pricing-engine config cfg-2290 changed cache.ttl_seconds 5 -> 4 at 09:20Z, cutting quote cache hit rate
Higher miss rate drives more pricing-engine calls to market-data-service and redis-cache, adding latency
order-service's pricing call path slows, contributing to p99 and 504s
order-service error rate steps ~31% at the 11:00Z bucket

assumptions: A TTL shortening would need to amplify load on an upstream that is already near saturation — not evidenced anywhere.
pricing-engine telemetry was never queried, so an induced regression there is speculative.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Timing is disqualifying: cfg-2290 applied at 09:20Z, ~100 minutes before the ~11:00Z onset (F16), yet the failure began abruptly as a step change, not gradually after 09:20Z. F3 scopes all failures to the exchange-gateway call on placeOrder, not to pricing/quote lookup; redis-cache cpu (F24) and market-data-service p99 (F25) are flat through the window with no step at 11:00Z.

facts.statement: order-service error_rate was flat ~0.2% (max ~0.3%) through the 10:52Z bucket, then stepped to 23.12% (max 31.9%) in the 11:00Z bucket and held ~31% (30.77-31.47%) through 12:52Z; latency_p99_ms stepped from ~147-153ms to 4054.96ms avg (max 5509.9) in the same bucket and remained ~5000-5400ms.
All 349 order-service ERROR logs (11:02:45Z-12:58:54Z) share a single signature: 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)' — the failure is scoped to the placeOrder operation.

exchange-gateway shows the same onset with larger magnitude: error_rate step from ~0.2% to 38.56% avg at 11:00Z (peaking ~48%) and latency_p99_ms from ~129ms to 4527.71ms avg; its log errors begin 11:01:25Z with connect timeouts to host=api.exchange-partner.example (op=placeOrder and op=quoteSnapshot) preceding 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable'.

exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate stepped from ~0.29-0.31% (10:30-10:54Z) to 11.36% avg/max 44.52% in the 10:58Z bucket and ~44-48% from 11:02Z onward, holding through 12:58Z; upstream_latency_ms stepped from ~117-122ms to 2385.07ms avg (max 9177.49) at 10:58Z and ~8900-9750ms from 11:02Z — a ~75x step.

Every host-attributed ERROR in exchange-gateway logs names the single external upstream api.exchange-partner.example: across the full WARN+ window (10:30-12:59Z, 309 matches) the only patterns are host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder (163) and op=quoteSnapshot (146); no other host value appears.

A second distinct ERROR signature is also attributed to the external partner: 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable (x-partner-request-id=...)' — 161 occurrences 10:30-12:59Z, first seen 11:02:20Z, still occurring 12:58:32Z.

Only one deployment occurred across all services in 06:00Z-12:59Z: order-service v2.15.2 at 10:48:00Z ('Add idempotency keys to order submit'), status rolled_back at 11:16:00Z. The only config change in the window is cfg-2290 on pricing-engine (cache.ttl_seconds 5->4) at 09:20:00Z.

Deploy/onset/rollback timeline: v2.15.2 deployed 10:48:00Z (precedes onset), order-service error onset ~11:00Z, exchange-gateway first ERROR 11:01:25Z, rollback 11:16:00Z; the config change is ~100 min before onset.
order-service local resource metrics are flat across the incident: db_pool_in_use 13.64-14.37 avg (max 15.49) and cpu_pct 39-40.7% avg with no step at 11:00Z.

ledger-db shows no resource step at or before 11:00Z: connections_active 60.22-63.07 avg (max 68.31) in every bucket 09:00-12:50Z, cpu_pct flat ~29-30%, and slow_queries_per_min ~1/min with the 11:00Z bucket actually slightly lower.

kafka shows no queue/replication degradation: under_replicated_partitions 0.0 avg and max in every bucket 09:00-12:50Z, messages_in_per_s ~2500 (mean 2523.82, no step at 11:00Z), cpu_pct flat ~34-36%.
redis-cache cpu_pct was flat ~22% (mean 22.02) with no sustained step at 11:00Z, and market-data-service latency_p99_ms was flat ~40ms across 09:00-12:59Z with no co-onset degradation.

order-service's dependency graph places exchange-gateway on the placeOrder path, and exchange-gateway depends on external exchange-api which has has_telemetry:false — the only node in the graph whose own availability cannot be confirmed from telemetry.

Three shared components sit in order-service's blast radius (ledger-db, kafka, redis-cache, all shared:true), and historical incidents matching 'order submit 504s after a release' have four different root causes — including HIST-103 (2025-10-21, external exchange API outage) with the same service pair and closest match_score 6.
exchange-gateway's upstream_error_rate and upstream_latency_ms are exposed only as a single aggregated series with no per-upstream-target dimension, so a by-target metric split cannot be produced.

assumptions: The external partner's own state at ~11:00Z is unobservable (has_telemetry:false, no change feed for the vendor endpoint), so no positive partner-side evidence exists; the external-origin conclusion rests on exclusion of internal causes plus rollback ineffectiveness and log attribution.
exchange-gateway's connect timeouts are causally prior to its 503s rather than a local gateway fault (the timeouts precede the 503s in the log stream).

The gateway's residual ~44% error rate vs order-service's ~31% reflects gateway traffic mix (the quoteSnapshot path is not consumed by order-service) rather than a second degraded upstream; this is inference from log attribution (F29-F31) and banding, not a per-target metric split (F26).

order-service endpoint isolation is inferred from log message text ('placeOrder' in all 349 ERROR lines); the metric-level split of errors by endpoint and order-service request_rate were not retrieved.
No feature-flag toggles occurred in the window: only cfg-2290 appears in the config-change query, but no feature-flag tool was available, so flag flips may be unrepresented rather than absent.
No unrecorded infra event (node drain, failover, scaling) occurred on a downstream dependency in the window; only versioned deploy/config records were queried, and infra event feeds were not.

The persistence of the failure past rollback (F15) is not attributable to a lingering side effect of v2.15.2 (e.g. poisoned state), since no mechanism for that is evidenced and the error signature points solely to the gateway-to-partner call.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) exchange-gateway's degradation precedes and is independent of order-service: its ERROR stream starts 11:01:25Z (earlier than order-service's first error at 11:02:45Z), includes 146 op=quoteSnapshot timeouts in addition to placeOrder, and its circuit breaker tripped OPEN for exchange-api (failure ratio 0.47 over 60s) at 11:03:26Z.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) No log evidence of a second failing internal upstream: a search for 'upstream error' in exchange-gateway over 10:30-12:59Z returned 0 matches, and 'host=' over 12:40-12:58Z returned only api.exchange-partner.example entries.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) The failure did not stop at rollback: order-service error_rate stayed ~31% and p99 ~5000-5400ms through 12:52Z, ~96 minutes after the 11:16Z rollback of v2.15.2, and persisted after the gateway's circuit breaker opened at 11:03:26Z.

timeline.event: No deployment and no config change recorded in any service between 2026-03-16T12:00Z and 2026-03-17T06:00Z (count 0), so the pre-incident baseline contains no other change.
cfg-2290 applied on pricing-engine: cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 ('Shorter quote cache TTL') by config-bot — ~100 min before the onset, later excluded on timing.
order-service v2.15.2 deployed by a.khan ('Add idempotency keys to order submit') — the only deployment in the whole incident window; later rolled back.

exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate steps from ~0.3% to 11.36% (max 44.52%) and upstream_latency_ms from ~120ms to 2385ms avg (max 9177ms) — the earliest metric onset, ~2 min before order-service's error onset.
order-service error_rate steps from ~0.2% to 23.12% (max 31.9%) and p99 steps from ~150ms to 4054.96ms (max 5509.9) — a ~30x latency step; error rate then holds ~31% through 12:52Z.

exchange-gateway error_rate rises to 38.56% avg and p99 to 4527.71ms avg. No step change in order-service local resources (pool 13.64-14.37, cpu ~39-40.7%) or in shared components (ledger-db, kafka, redis-cache, market-data-service all flat).
exchange-gateway's first ERROR: connect timeouts to host=api.exchange-partner.example on op=placeOrder and op=quoteSnapshot — 70 seconds before order-service's first error.
First 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable (x-partner-request-id=...)' in exchange-gateway — the external partner returning 503; still occurring at 12:58:32Z (161 total occurrences).
order-service's first ERROR log: 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)'; all 349 order-service ERROR lines in the incident share this single signature.
exchange-gateway circuit breaker trips OPEN for exchange-api (failure ratio 0.47 over 60s).
order-service v2.15.2 rolled back — the failure does not abate.
order-service error_rate still ~31% (30.77-31.47%) and p99 ~5000-5400ms — ~96 minutes after rollback, decisively excluding the release as root cause.

exchange-gateway still degrading: upstream_error_rate ~43.65-47.51%, upstream_latency_ms ~9.1-9.5s; only host value appearing in logs remains api.exchange-partner.example, and zero 'upstream error' matches over the whole window.

recommended_actions.action: Stop treating the order-service release as the fix: the v2.15.2 rollback at 11:16Z did not change the failure (F15) — keep it rolled back but do not expect mitigation from further order-service rollbacks or restarts; redirect on-call effort to the exchange-gateway -> api.exchange-partner.example path.
recommended_actions.rationale: Error rate stayed ~31% and p99 ~5000-5400ms for ~96 minutes after the rollback, so the change surface / rollback axis is a dead end.

recommended_actions.action: Engage the external exchange partner (api.exchange-partner.example) immediately with the captured evidence: the exchange-gateway ERROR lines showing connect timeouts to host=api.exchange-partner.example (op=placeOrder and op=quoteSnapshot) and the partner's own 503 responses carrying x-partner-request-id values (161 occurrences, still occurring at 12:58:32Z) — ask for their incident/status for the 10:58Z-13:00Z window.
recommended_actions.rationale: All gateway degradation is attributed to this single host; the partner has has_telemetry:false so its status can only be confirmed by the vendor. The x-partner-request-id values give the vendor a direct trace handle.

recommended_actions.action: On exchange-gateway, treat the open circuit breaker (tripped 11:03:26Z, failure ratio 0.47 over 60s) as a live mitigation: confirm it is still/stably OPEN for the exchange-api upstream and that order-service workloads are degrading gracefully (fast fail or queue) rather than hanging on ~9s upstream latency, to avoid burning order-service thread/connection budget.
recommended_actions.rationale: Gateway upstream_latency_ms is ~9.1-9.5s and upstream_error_rate ~44-48% and holding; the gateway is the only internal component between order-service and the failing partner. Note upstream_error_rate series are only available in aggregate (no per-target label), so verification must use the breaker state and gateway logs.

recommended_actions.action: Prepare a customer/order-impact mitigation decision on the placeOrder path: since 100% of order-service's ERRORs are the exchange-gateway 504 on placeOrder (F3), consider backpressure, queuing, or deferring submits until the partner recovers, and verify the api-gateway -> order-service edge is shedding rather than amplifying load.
recommended_actions.rationale: All 349 order-service ERROR lines are the single placeOrder/exchange-gateway 504 signature, so the blast radius is the submit path specifically rather than all endpoints.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm partner recovery before declaring the incident closed: watch exchange-gateway upstream_latency_ms (baseline ~117-122ms) and upstream_error_rate (baseline ~0.3%) return to pre-10:58Z levels, and confirm order-service error_rate returns to ~0.2% and p99 to ~150ms with no further placeOrder/exchange-gateway 504s.
recommended_actions.rationale: These are the measured baseline-vs-incident values on both sides of the failing hop; recovery must be visible in both the gateway's upstream metrics and order-service's error/latency metrics.

recommended_actions.action: Add (or document the absence of) per-upstream-target dimensions to exchange-gateway's upstream_error_rate / upstream_latency_ms metrics, so future incidents can split blame by upstream target instead of relying on log attribution.
recommended_actions.rationale: F26 records that these metrics expose only a single aggregate series with no target label, which is why the ~44% gateway vs ~31% order-service gap stays an inference rather than a measured split.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument or contractually monitor the external partner endpoint (api.exchange-partner.example) — currently has_telemetry:false — e.g. a synthetic probe or vendor SLO feed, so partner-side outages are positively evidenced rather than inferred.
recommended_actions.rationale: The only node on the path whose own availability cannot be confirmed from telemetry; closing this gap removes the main reason confidence is medium rather than high.

recommended_actions.action: Harden order-service against exchange-gateway/partner degradation: short, explicit timeouts on the placeOrder -> exchange-gateway call, bounded retries, and bulkhead/queueing so a partner-side 9s upstream latency cannot push order submit into 504s at 31% with a 30x p99 step.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failure propagated from ~9s gateway upstream latency to ~5s order-service p99 and 504s on the submit path; a resilient client boundary would contain partner degradation.

recommended_actions.action: Update the on-call runbook and the post-incident review to lead with the dependency check: for 'order submit 504s after a release', check exchange-gateway/partner before rolling back, since symptom match is not cause match (HIST-103 is the closest precedent with the same service pair).
recommended_actions.rationale: Historical precedents with the same symptom have four different root causes; in this incident the rollback was ineffective and cost ~28 minutes of the incident window.

recommended_actions.action: Before closing, run the cheap discriminating checks that were never completed, to tighten the medium confidence: order-service endpoint-level error split and request_rate; ledger-db disk_used_pct and replication_lag_ms; redis-cache evictions/memory/connected_clients; and any internal infra event feed (node restarts/drains/scaling) for the 10:45-11:05Z window.
recommended_actions.rationale: These are the residual gaps behind H1's assumptions — they cannot reorder H1 vs H4 per the reviewed analysis, but they convert the exclusion-based reasoning into direct evidence.

data_gaps: No telemetry exists for the external partner (api.exchange-partner.example has has_telemetry:false and no change feed), so its state at ~11:00Z is unobservable and the external-origin conclusion rests on exclusion of internal causes plus rollback ineffectiveness, not on positive partner-side evidence.

exchange-gateway's upstream_error_rate/upstream_latency_ms are single aggregated series with no per-target dimension (F26), so the gateway's residual ~44% error rate vs order-service's ~31% cannot be split by upstream via metrics; the one-victim reading is log-based inference.

order-service request_rate and the metric-level split of errors by endpoint were not retrieved; placeOrder isolation is inferred only from log message text, so the fraction of total traffic affected cannot be quantified.

order-service 'restarts' metric was not queried and the v2.15.2 deploy time is not evidenced in telemetry, so deploy-precedes-onset is established from the change record plus error timing (F14) rather than from telemetry.
No feature-flag tooling was available; only cfg-2290 appeared in the config-change query, so flag toggles may be unrepresented rather than absent.

No internal infra/deployment event feed (node restarts, drains, scaling, failovers) was queried for any dependency, and deployment queries for pricing-engine and exchange-gateway returned no records — only versioned changes are excluded, not invisible infra events.
redis-cache evictions_per_min, memory_pct and connected_clients were never retrieved (only cpu_pct), so redis memory-pressure/eviction exhaustion is not fully excluded.
ledger-db disk_used_pct and replication_lag_ms were never queried (pool, cpu and slow-query signals are confirmed flat), so disk-fill or replica-lag on ledger-db is not fully excluded.
kafka consumer lag/queue depth was not queried; only broker-side health (under_replicated_partitions 0.0, messages_in_per_s ~2500, cpu flat) is confirmed.
market-data-service error_rate was not retrieved — only its latency_p99_ms is shown flat.
No metric or log data was retrieved for pricing-engine itself, so any latent effect of cfg-2290 beyond its 09:20Z timing is unexcluded.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that exchange-gateway's failing upstream calls also include a non-partner internal target (e.g. 'host=' or 'upstream error' log lines naming another host), which would break the single-victim attribution and reopen H4-style internal causes.
A partner-side statement or status page showing the partner was healthy 10:58-13:00Z, which would invalidate the external root cause outright.

Discovery of an unrecorded internal infra event (node drain, failover, scaling) on exchange-gateway or a shared component coinciding with 10:58-11:00Z, which would re-open H4 despite flat resource metrics.
A per-target metric split showing gateway errors distributed across multiple upstreams rather than concentrated on api.exchange-partner.example.

Evidence that the persistent post-rollback failure (F15) is a lingering side effect of v2.15.2 (e.g. poisoned state, unstuck lock, duplicate-submit queue) rather than continued partner degradation, which would revive H2.

Occurrence of the same partner-attributed exchange-gateway timeouts/503s in a window with order-service v2.15.2 absent (before 10:48Z or after rollback) — actually supportive of H1, but absence of them in a partner-failure window would contradict it.

Any change record (deploy, config, feature flag) on order-service, exchange-gateway, api-gateway or a shared component that falls inside the 10:58-11:01Z onset window, overturning the 'no internal change surface' exclusion.

findings.statement: Only one deployment occurred across ALL services in the incident window (2026-03-17T06:00Z–12:59Z): order-service v2.15.2, deployed 2026-03-17T10:48:00Z by a.khan, summary 'Add idempotency keys to order submit', status 'rolled_back', rolled back at 2026-03-17T11:16:00Z.

No deployment and no config change was recorded in any service between 2026-03-16T12:00Z and 2026-03-17T06:00Z (count 0 in both queries), so the pre-incident baseline day contains no other change that could explain an onset before 06:00Z.

The single window config change is cfg-2290 on pricing-engine: cache.ttl_seconds changed 5 -> 4 at 2026-03-17T09:20:00Z by config-bot ('Shorter quote cache TTL'), i.e. ~52 min after the v2.15.2 deploy and ~88 min before the deploy was rolled back.

order-service's dependency graph: edge direction is caller->callee, so upstream caller is api-gateway->order-service (http); order-service's downstream edges are to ledger-db (db), pricing-engine (http), exchange-gateway (http) and kafka (queue-produce); pricing-engine further depends on market-data-service (http) and redis-cache (cache); exchange-gateway depends on external exchange-api which has has_telemetry:false.

Three shared components sit in order-service's blast radius: ledger-db (postgres), kafka (kafka) and redis-cache (redis, reached via pricing-engine), all owned by platform and flagged shared:true — meaning other services can affect order-service through them.

findings.statement: Historical incidents matching 'order submit 504s / high error after a release' have four DIFFERENT root causes, so symptom match is not cause match: HIST-103 (2025-10-21) 504 on order submit from external exchange API outage; HIST-101 (2025-08-14) auth-service release raised bcrypt cost 10->14; HIST-116 (2025-12-18) gateway envoy upgrade changed HTTP/2 max concurrent streams default; HIST-102 (2025-09-02) unplanned ledger-db primary failover and HIST-110 (2026-01-15) ledger-db IOPS throttling, both matching 'order latency'/'504 at gateway'.

findings.statement: The entire change surface in 2026-03-17T06:00Z–12:59Z is one deployment (order-service v2.15.2, deployed 10:48Z, 'Add idempotency keys to order submit', status rolled_back at 11:16Z) and one config change (pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 at 09:20Z). Re-querying the narrower 09:00–13:00Z window returns exactly the same two items, count 1 each, so no other service, dependency or shared-component release/flag change is hidden by bucketing.

Deploy→onset→rollback timeline: v2.15.2 deployed 10:48:00Z; order-service error onset ~11:00Z (inline with T1's 23–31% jump); exchange-gateway's first ERROR at 11:01:25Z; rollback at 11:16:00Z. The gap between deploy and onset is ~12 min, and the deploy precedes the onset.

Decisive timing signal against v2.15.2 as root cause: the failure did not stop at the rollback. order-service error_rate stayed ~31% (30.77–31.47%) and p99 ~5000–5400ms through 12:52Z, i.e. ~96 minutes AFTER the 11:16:00Z rollback, and the same persisted after exchange-gateway's circuit breaker opened at 11:03:26Z. A release-attributable fault would normally abate at rollback; this one did not.

Blast radius by shared component: order-service's dependency graph shows downstream edges to ledger-db (db, shared), pricing-engine (http) -> redis-cache (cache, shared), exchange-gateway (http) -> external exchange-api (has_telemetry:false), and kafka (queue-produce, shared); upstream caller api-gateway -> order-service. The changed config (pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds) is 88 min before the rollback and 100 min before onset, so it cannot be the onset trigger.

findings.statement: ledger-db shows NO resource step change at or before ~11:00Z. connections_active held 60.22–63.07 avg (max 68.31) in every 10-min bucket from 09:00Z through 12:50Z, with no jump at the 11:00Z bucket (62.13 avg) — pool/connection saturation is absent.

ledger-db cpu_pct was flat ~29–30% across the entire 09:00–12:59Z window (mean 29.97, min 26.58, max 33.22, missing_points 0); the 11:00Z bucket avg 29.98 is identical to the 09:00Z bucket. No step change.

ledger-db slow_queries_per_min remained ~1/min throughout (mean 1.01), with the 11:00Z bucket at 0.96 and 11:10Z at 0.9 — actually slightly LOWER during the incident, the opposite of IO/query degradation. No IOPS/slow-query step change.

kafka shows no queue/replication degradation: under_replicated_partitions was 0.0 avg and 0.0 max in every single bucket 09:00Z–12:50Z (min 0.0, max 0.0, mean 0.0), and messages_in_per_s stayed ~2500 msg/s (mean 2523.82) with no step at 11:00Z (2540.31 avg).
kafka cpu_pct was flat ~34–36% across the window (mean 34.94, min 30.64, max 38.66); the 11:00Z bucket avg 35.85 and 11:10Z 35.44 are within baseline noise. No step change.

redis-cache cpu_pct was flat ~22% (mean 22.02, min 19.65, max 24.53) with no step at the 11:00Z bucket (22.75 avg vs 21.91 at 10:50Z and 21.63 at 11:10Z) — the single bucket bump is within baseline noise, not a sustained step change.

market-data-service latency_p99_ms was flat ~40ms across 09:00–12:59Z (mean 40.14, min 35.38, max 44.57); the 11:00Z bucket avg 39.85 is unchanged from baseline. If reachable, this upstream data source shows no co-onset latency degradation.

exchange-gateway's upstream_error_rate and upstream_latency_ms are exposed only as single aggregated series — the metrics API returns no per-upstream-target breakdown dimension (available_metrics lists just 'upstream_error_rate' and 'upstream_latency_ms' with no target label), so a by-target comparison of api.exchange-partner.example vs other upstreams cannot be produced from metrics.

exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate stepped from ~0.29-0.31% (10:30-10:54Z buckets) to 11.36% avg/max 44.52% in the 10:58Z 4-min bucket, and to ~44-48% (avg 45.16, max 46.7) from 11:02Z onward, holding ~43.65-47.51% through the 12:58Z bucket.

exchange-gateway upstream_latency_ms stepped from ~117-122ms (10:30-10:54Z) to 2385.07ms avg (max 9177.49) at the 10:58Z bucket and to ~8900-9750ms avg from 11:02Z onward, remaining ~9.1-9.5s through 12:58Z — a ~75x step change coincident with the 10:58Z error onset.

Every host-attributed ERROR in exchange-gateway logs names the single external upstream api.exchange-partner.example. In the full WARN+ window (10:30-12:59Z, 309 matches) the only two patterns are 'host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder' (163) and 'host=api.exchange-partner.example op=quoteSnapshot' (146); no other host value appears in the ERROR stream.

findings.statement: The second, distinct ERROR signature is also attributed to the external partner: 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable (x-partner-request-id=...)' — 161 occurrences over 10:30-12:59Z, first seen 11:02:20Z, and still occurring at 12:58:32Z (25 in the 12:40-12:58Z slice alone). 'exchange-api' here is the external partner (exchange-partner.example), not a second internal upstream.

No log evidence of a second failing internal upstream: a targeted search for 'upstream error' in exchange-gateway over 10:30-12:59Z returned 0 matches, and a query for 'host=' over 12:40-12:58Z returned only api.exchange-partner.example entries. All gateway degradation in the window is attributable to the one external partner host.
